title: Right cancellation for right-anodyne monomorphisms
statement: Use simplicial sets and simplicial maps of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and right anodyne maps of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne], in any fixed containing universe. Let $f:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $g:B\hookrightarrow C$ be degreewise injective simplicial maps. Assume that $f$ is right anodyne. Then $g$ is right anodyne if and only if $g\circ f$ is right anodyne. No quasicategory or Kan hypothesis is imposed on $A,B,C$.

source.place: Corollary 4.1.10, printed p.140 (PDF p.155, zero-based). Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this one-sided simplicial cancellation theorem.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-right-anodyne-lifting-characterization], a simplicial map is right anodyne in the sense of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne] if and only if it has the left lifting property against every right fibration of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Both directions are used below: the forward direction for $gf$ in Step 2 and for the pushout-product map in Step 4, and the converse for $g$ in Step 5.

source.place: Corollary 4.1.10, printed p.140; the lifting characterization of right anodyne maps is cited as a node of its own

proof.text: If $g$ is right anodyne, so is $gf$: the composite is the transfinite composition of the length-two chain $A\xrightarrow f B\xrightarrow g C$, so this is directly the composition closure in [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. For the converse assume $gf$ is right anodyne. Let $q:E\to S$ be any right fibration and choose a lifting square for $g$, given by $a:B\to E$ and $b:C\to S$ with $qa=bg$. Step 1 applied to $gf$ gives $h:C\to E$ such that $hgf=af$ and $qh=b$. Thus $a$ and $hg$ have exactly the same restriction along $f$ and the same composite with $q$.

source.place: Corollary 4.1.10, printed p.140; explicit agent lifting argument, composition direction and the initial lift for the converse

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] to the right anodyne map $f$ and the right fibration $q$. The restriction map $\rho:\operatorname{Fun}(B,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,S)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,S)}\operatorname{Fun}(A,E)$ is a trivial Kan fibration. The vertices $a$ and $hg$ have the same image $(bg,af)$. Use the boundary lifting property for $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ from [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], with upper endpoints $a,hg$ and lower map the constant edge at $(bg,af)$. The lift is a map $H:B\times\Delta^1\to E$ satisfying $H|_{B\times\{0\}}=a$, $H|_{B\times\{1\}}=hg$, $qH=bg\,\mathrm{pr}_B$, and $H(f\times1)=af\,\mathrm{pr}_A$. The product interpretation is the defining formula for the internal functor simplicial set in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Corollary 4.1.10, printed p.140; explicit agent lifting argument, homotopy correcting the restriction of the initial lift

proof.text: The endpoint inclusion $e:\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ is the right horn $\Lambda_1^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$, hence right anodyne by [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. Since $g$ is a monomorphism, [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product], with first variable $e$ and second variable $g$, gives a right anodyne map whose domain is $(\{1\}\times C)\amalg_{\{1\}\times B}(\Delta^1\times B)$ and whose codomain is $\Delta^1\times C$. In each degree the bijections $(t,x)\mapsto(x,t)$ commute with all simplicial operators and with the two gluing inclusions. They therefore induce an isomorphism of this pushout diagram with the diagram defining $j:(B\times\Delta^1)\amalg_{B\times\{1\}}(C\times\{1\})\to C\times\Delta^1$. The map $j$ is right anodyne because conjugation by isomorphisms preserves the class: such a conjugate is a finite composite of the original map and two isomorphisms, all in the class of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. The maps $H$ and $h$ agree on $B\times\{1\}$ because $H_1=hg$, so they define a map from this pushout to $E$. Its composite with $q$ agrees with the restriction of $b\,\mathrm{pr}_C$. Step 1 gives an extension $\widetilde H:C\times\Delta^1\to E$ over $S$. Put $c=\widetilde H|_{C\times\{0\}}$. Then $cg=H_0=a$ and $qc=b$, giving the requested diagonal in the arbitrary lifting square for $g$. Notice that the prescribed map on $C$ is at endpoint $1$, precisely the endpoint allowed by the right-horn convention.

source.place: Corollary 4.1.10, printed p.140; explicit agent lifting argument, extend the correcting homotopy using the final-endpoint pushout product

proof.text: Step 4 proves that $g$ has the left lifting property against every right fibration. The converse direction of the characterization in Step 1 therefore makes $g$ right anodyne. Together with Step 2 this proves the claimed equivalence. The argument used only the right anodyne hypothesis on $f$, the right anodyne hypothesis on $gf$ for the reverse direction, and the degreewise injectivity of $g$ in the pushout-product application; it imposed no Kan or quasicategory hypothesis on $A,B,C$.

source.place: Corollary 4.1.10, printed p.140; explicit agent lifting argument, conclude by the lifting characterization
